# NodeToCode MCP tool reference

<!-- Generated by the N2CToolReference commandlet from the NodeToCode MCP tool registry. Do not edit: run Scripts/generate_tool_reference.py. -->

NodeToCode registers 67 MCP tools in 12 toolsets. The same data, with each tool's full input and output schema, is in [tools.generated.json](tools.generated.json).

What `tools/list` shows depends on Project Settings > Plugins > Node to Code (see "Tool Profiles and Toolsets" in [AGENTS-mcp-server.md](AGENTS-mcp-server.md)):

- Tool Profile Default toolsets, Tool Exposure List every tool (the defaults): the 64 tools marked Default below. `run-python`, `save-python-script` and `delete-python-script` are listed too when the per-user Allow MCP Python Execution is on.
- Tool Exposure Tool search: only `call_tool`, `describe_toolset`, `list_toolsets` ([below](#tool-search-meta-tools)), which reach the same tools.
- Tool Profile Python scripting only: the tools of `PythonTools`; Custom: the toolsets named in Custom Toolsets.
- On UE 5.8 with Epic's Unreal MCP (ModelContextProtocol and EditorToolset enabled), Overlapping Tools set to Automatic and the Default toolsets profile, the tools that name an Unreal MCP counterpart below are left to Unreal MCP and not served ([NodeToCode and Epic tool mapping](../../wiki/developers/NodeToCode-and-Epic-Tool-Mapping.md)). This reference lists every tool on every engine.

Annotations are MCP behaviour hints; "unset" means the tool sends none and a client assumes the MCP default. "Untrusted text" marks results that carry text from the project's Blueprints. "During PIE" says whether the tool still runs while a Play In Editor session does (others are refused with PIE_ACTIVE). "Default" means the shipped settings serve the tool.

## BlueprintDiscoveryTools

Find and read Blueprints: the Blueprint focused in the editor, open Blueprint editors, a Blueprint's graphs and functions, the functions it can override, and the node types a graph can use. Graphs are returned as N2C JSON.

### export-n2cjson-batch

**Export N2C JSON for many graphs**

Exports many Blueprint graphs as N2C JSON in one call, one file per graph, with no Blueprint editor open and without changing focus. Select the graphs with targets [{blueprintPath, graphName?, graphGuid?}] (a target with only blueprintPath exports every graph of that Blueprint that has nodes) or with a tag and/or category (tag-blueprint-graph). Each file holds the document get-blueprint-n2cjson returns for that graph. The files go to one folder under Saved/NodeToCode/Exports (outDir, or a new Batch_&lt;time&gt; folder); the result lists each file {path, bytes, estimatedTokens, nodeCount} and each target that failed with its code. Read the files in parts with read-file. Assets that are not Blueprints are refused per target (UNSUPPORTED_ASSET_TYPE).

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | yes | yes | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `targets` | `array<object>` | no |  | The graphs to work on: [{blueprintPath, graphName?, graphGuid?}]. Give targets, or tag and/or category, not both. At most 200 graphs per call. A path that is not a Blueprint (a Material, a Data Asset) fails with UNSUPPORTED_ASSET_TYPE. |
| `tag` | `string` | no |  | Instead of targets: every graph with this tag (tag-blueprint-graph, list-blueprint-tags), in category when given. |
| `category` | `string` | no |  | Instead of targets: every graph tagged in this category (with tag: that tag in this category). |
| `depth` | `integer` | no |  | Optional, 0 to 5. Each file also captures the functions, macros and collapsed graphs its graph uses up to this many calls away. Default: the project's Max Translation Depth setting. |
| `compact` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Optional, default true. No whitespace; false indents the JSON. |
| `outDir` | `string` | no |  | Optional. A folder name under Saved/NodeToCode/Exports for the files (letters, digits, _ - . and up to four parts joined by /). Exporting the same graphs to the same outDir again replaces their files. Default: a new Batch_&lt;date-time&gt; folder. |

### get-blueprint-n2cjson

**Read a Blueprint as N2C JSON**

Reads any Blueprint in the project as NodeToCode's N2C JSON by asset path, with no Blueprint editor open and without changing focus: one graph (graphName or graphGuid, see list-blueprint-graphs) or, with neither, every graph of the Blueprint in one document. The document is the one get-focused-blueprint returns (nodes and pins with ids {short, guid}, flows, the guids table). When it would exceed about 20000 tokens, or with toFile, it is written to a file under Saved/NodeToCode/Exports and the result is {path, bytes, estimatedTokens, reason, graphCount, nodeCount}: read that file in parts.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | yes | yes | yes |

Client hints: kept loaded when a client defers tools (`anthropic/alwaysLoad`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | yes |  | Required. Asset path of the Blueprint, e.g. /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door or /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door.BP_Door. |
| `graphName` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Name of one graph (event graph, function, macro, collapsed, delegate or interface graph). With neither graphName nor graphGuid, every graph is read. |
| `graphGuid` | `string` | no |  | Optional. The graph's GraphGuid from list-blueprint-graphs (a function's ID); stable across renames. Wins over graphName. |
| `depth` | `integer` | no |  | Optional, 0 to 5. Also capture the functions, macros and collapsed graphs the graph uses up to this many calls away (Max Translation Depth). Default: the project's Max Translation Depth setting. |
| `compact` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Optional, default true. No whitespace; false indents the JSON as get-focused-blueprint does. |
| `toFile` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Optional, default false. Always write the document to a file and return its path. |

### get-editor-context

**Read what the user is looking at**

Returns what the user is looking at in the Unreal Editor, in one call: the focused Blueprint (the Blueprint editor the user last activated) and its focused graph (name, graphGuid, type), the GUIDs of the nodes selected in that graph, every open Blueprint editor (Widget and Animation Blueprints included) with the graph it shows, unsaved changes and compile status, whether Play In Editor is running, and the engine version. Reads only; opens and focuses nothing. Pass the graphGuid to get-blueprint-n2cjson or the graph tools.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | yes | yes | yes |

No arguments.

Returns `structuredContent` matching its `outputSchema` (in tools.generated.json).

### get-focused-blueprint

**Read the focused Blueprint graph**

Collects and serializes the currently focused Blueprint graph in the Unreal Editor into NodeToCode's N2CJSON format. The focused Blueprint is the Blueprint editor the user last activated (clicked its tab or inside it) or that open-blueprint-asset last opened; the graph is the one that editor shows. To read a Blueprint without opening or focusing it, or a graph too large for one result, use get-blueprint-n2cjson.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | yes | yes | yes |

Client hints: text results up to 200000 characters (`anthropic/maxResultSizeChars`); kept loaded when a client defers tools (`anthropic/alwaysLoad`).

No arguments.

Returns `structuredContent` matching its `outputSchema` (in tools.generated.json).

### get-open-blueprint-editors

**List open Blueprint editors**

Returns every open Blueprint editor (Widget and Animation Blueprint editors included) with its asset path, its graphs (event graphs, functions, macros, interface implementations and delegate signatures, each with graphGuid and type), the graph it shows, whether it is the focused editor, unsaved changes (packageDirty) and compile status. For the focused graph and the selected nodes in one call, use get-editor-context.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |

No arguments.

Returns `structuredContent` matching its `outputSchema` (in tools.generated.json).

### list-blueprint-functions

**List Blueprint functions**

Lists what a Blueprint defines that runs as a function: its function graphs (overrides included), its interface function graphs, its custom events and its override and interface events, with their parameters and metadata

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | yes | yes | yes |

Unreal MCP counterpart (UE 5.8): `BlueprintTools.list_functions, list_graphs`. Left to Unreal MCP by default when it runs in the same editor (Overlapping Tools).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | no |  | Asset path of the Blueprint (e.g., '/Game/Blueprints/MyActor.MyActor'). If not provided, uses focused Blueprint. |

### list-blueprint-graphs

**List Blueprint graphs**

Lists every graph of any Blueprint in the project by asset path, with no Blueprint editor open: name, graphGuid (stable across renames; pass it to get-blueprint-n2cjson or the graph tools), kind (event, function, macro, collapsed, delegate, interface), nodeCount, readOnly (shown read-only in the Blueprint editor) and, for a collapsed graph, parentGraph.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | yes | yes | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | yes |  | Required. Asset path of the Blueprint, e.g. /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door or /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door.BP_Door. |

Returns `structuredContent` matching its `outputSchema` (in tools.generated.json).

### list-overridable-functions

**List overridable functions**

Lists the functions a Blueprint can override from its parent classes and its interfaces (its own and its parents'), as the editor's Override menu does. functionType says how to implement one: Event as an event node in an event graph, Function as a function graph; isImplemented counts event nodes, function graphs and interface graphs

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | yes | yes | yes |

Unreal MCP counterpart (UE 5.8): `BlueprintTools.list_functions, list_events`. Left to Unreal MCP by default when it runs in the same editor (Overlapping Tools).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | no |  | Asset path of the Blueprint (e.g., '/Game/Blueprints/MyActor.MyActor'). If not provided, uses focused Blueprint. |
| `includeImplemented` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Whether to include functions that are already implemented/overridden |
| `filterByCategory` | `string` | no |  | Filter functions by category (e.g., 'Input', 'Collision', 'Animation') |
| `searchTerm` | `string` | no |  | Search term to filter function names |

### search-blueprint-nodes

**Search Blueprint node actions**

Searches for Blueprint nodes/actions relevant to a given query, in the action list of the target graph (blueprintPath, graphName, graphGuid, or the focused graph): the list the editor's node menu shows with Context Sensitive off. For common math operations, you can simply search for symbols like '+', '-', '*', or '/'. The promotable math nodes (e.g., Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide) typically have wildcard pins that automatically promote to compatible types (e.g., float, integer, vector), so you usually don't need to search for type-specific versions like 'multiply float by float'. Read-only: it never changes the graph. Each result's spawnMetadata.actionIdentifier is a stable ID (the node spawner's signature, the same in every search) to pass to add-bp-node-to-active-graph unchanged, with spawnMetadata.nodeName as nodeName.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | yes | yes | yes |

Unreal MCP counterpart (UE 5.8): `BlueprintTools.find_node_types, find_node_categories, get_node_type_pins`. Left to Unreal MCP by default when it runs in the same editor (Overlapping Tools).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `searchTerm` | `string` | yes |  | The text query to search for |
| `contextSensitive` | `boolean` | no | `true` | Kept for compatibility: true and false search the same list, the target graph's (as the editor's node menu with Context Sensitive off), and only set spawnMetadata.isContextSensitive. Both need a target graph. |
| `maxResults` | `integer` | no | `20` | Maximum number of results to return |
| `category` | `string` | no |  | Filter results by category. Common categories include: 'flowcontrol' (Branch, Sequence, etc.), 'operators' (math operators like +, -, *, /), 'struct' (Make/Break struct nodes), 'casting' (Cast nodes), 'math' (math functions). Case-insensitive partial match. |
| `excludeVMFunctions` | `boolean` | no | `true` | If true (default), excludes low-level VM math functions that are rarely used directly (e.g., type-specific math like 'Multiply_FloatFloat'). Set to false to include all results. |
| `blueprintContext` | `object` | no |  | The older form of blueprintPath plus graphName, used only when none of blueprintPath, graphName and graphGuid is given. The graph to search for. Without it (and without blueprintPath, graphName, graphGuid) the focused graph is used. A Blueprint or graph that does not exist is an error (ASSET_NOT_FOUND, GRAPH_NOT_FOUND), never a search in another context |
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Asset path of the Blueprint, e.g. /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door.BP_Door. With no target argument the focused graph is used; with blueprintPath alone, its focused graph or else its event graph. The result's 'target' says which graph was used. |
| `graphName` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Name of the graph (a function, macro, event graph or collapsed graph) in blueprintPath, or in the focused Blueprint without blueprintPath. AMBIGUOUS_GRAPH_NAME when two graphs share it: pass graphGuid then. |
| `graphGuid` | `string` | no |  | Optional. The graph's GUID (target.graphGuid of an earlier result; a function's functionGuid/guid is its graph GUID). Stable across renames and moves. Wins over graphName. |

## BlueprintGraphTools

Edit the nodes of a Blueprint graph: find, add and delete nodes, connect pins, set input pin values and add comment boxes.

### add-bp-node-to-active-graph

**Add a Blueprint node**

Adds a Blueprint node to a graph: the one blueprintPath plus graphName or graphGuid name, else the focused graph (the result's target says which). IMPORTANT: Use search-blueprint-nodes first and pass a result's spawnMetadata.actionIdentifier (a stable ID) and spawnMetadata.nodeName. NEXT STEP: After adding a node, use the 'connect-pins' tool to wire the node's pins to other nodes using the pinGuid values returned in inputPins and outputPins arrays. Refused with PIE_ACTIVE while a Play In Editor session runs; stop PIE first.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | no | no | no | no | no | no | yes |

Unreal MCP counterpart (UE 5.8): `BlueprintTools.create_node, write_graph_dsl`. Left to Unreal MCP by default when it runs in the same editor (Overlapping Tools).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nodeName` | `string` | yes |  | The node's menu name, spawnMetadata.nodeName of the search result (e.g., 'Spawn Actor from Class'). Only used to tell apart actions that share an actionIdentifier |
| `actionIdentifier` | `string` | yes |  | The stable action ID from spawnMetadata.actionIdentifier of a search-blueprint-nodes result, passed unchanged, e.g. (FieldName="/Script/Engine.KismetSystemLibrary:PrintString",NodeName="/Script/BlueprintGraph.K2Node_CallFunction"). It is the node spawner's signature, so it stays valid across searches, captures and compiles. Old search-text identifiers are still accepted for now. |
| `location` | `object` | no |  | The location to spawn the node at |
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Asset path of the Blueprint, e.g. /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door.BP_Door. With no target argument the focused graph is used; with blueprintPath alone, its focused graph or else its event graph. The result's 'target' says which graph was used. |
| `graphName` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Name of the graph (a function, macro, event graph or collapsed graph) in blueprintPath, or in the focused Blueprint without blueprintPath. AMBIGUOUS_GRAPH_NAME when two graphs share it: pass graphGuid then. |
| `graphGuid` | `string` | no |  | Optional. The graph's GUID (target.graphGuid of an earlier result; a function's functionGuid/guid is its graph GUID). Stable across renames and moves. Wins over graphName. |

### connect-pins

**Connect pins**

Connect pins between nodes of a Blueprint graph (the one blueprintPath plus graphName or graphGuid name, else the focused graph) using their GUIDs, in one undo transaction. A data output and an exec input take any number of links; a data input and an exec output take one, and a connection that would replace that link fails unless options.breakExistingLinks is true. Failed connections are listed in the result, which is not an error. Refused with PIE_ACTIVE while a Play In Editor session runs; stop PIE first.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | yes | yes | no | no | no | no | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `connections` | `array<object>` | yes |  | Array of pin connections to create |
| `options` | `object` | no |  |  |
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Asset path of the Blueprint, e.g. /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door.BP_Door. With no target argument the focused graph is used; with blueprintPath alone, its focused graph or else its event graph. The result's 'target' says which graph was used. |
| `graphName` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Name of the graph (a function, macro, event graph or collapsed graph) in blueprintPath, or in the focused Blueprint without blueprintPath. AMBIGUOUS_GRAPH_NAME when two graphs share it: pass graphGuid then. |
| `graphGuid` | `string` | no |  | Optional. The graph's GUID (target.graphGuid of an earlier result; a function's functionGuid/guid is its graph GUID). Stable across renames and moves. Wins over graphName. |

### create-comment-node

**Create a comment around nodes**

Creates a comment node around specified Blueprint nodes using their GUIDs, in the graph blueprintPath plus graphName or graphGuid name, else the focused graph. Get node GUIDs from find-nodes-in-graph or get-focused-blueprint first. Do NOT set a color unless the user requests it. Refused with PIE_ACTIVE while a Play In Editor session runs; stop PIE first.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | no | no | no | no | no | no | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `commentText` | `string` | no |  |  |
| `color` | `object` | no |  | RGB color values (0-1 range) |
| `fontSize` | `number` | no |  |  |
| `moveMode` | `string` | no | `"group"` | Movement mode for the comment. One of: `"group"`, `"none"`. |
| `padding` | `number` | no |  |  |
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Asset path of the Blueprint, e.g. /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door.BP_Door. With no target argument the focused graph is used; with blueprintPath alone, its focused graph or else its event graph. The result's 'target' says which graph was used. |
| `graphName` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Name of the graph (a function, macro, event graph or collapsed graph) in blueprintPath, or in the focused Blueprint without blueprintPath. AMBIGUOUS_GRAPH_NAME when two graphs share it: pass graphGuid then. |
| `graphGuid` | `string` | no |  | Optional. The graph's GUID (target.graphGuid of an earlier result; a function's functionGuid/guid is its graph GUID). Stable across renames and moves. Wins over graphName. |

### delete-blueprint-node

**Delete Blueprint nodes**

Deletes one or more Blueprint nodes from a graph using their GUIDs: the graph blueprintPath plus graphName or graphGuid name, else the focused graph. Supports connection preservation and batch operations. Refused with PIE_ACTIVE while a Play In Editor session runs; stop PIE first.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | yes | yes | no | no | no | no | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nodeGuids` | `array<string>` | yes |  | Array of node GUIDs to delete |
| `preserveConnections` | `boolean` | no | `false` | If true, reconnects the links that pass through each deleted node: the sources of its exec input to the targets of its exec output (only on a node with one exec input and one exec output), and through reroute knots. Each link made is listed in preservedConnections; a link the schema refuses or that would replace another link is not made. Data pins of other nodes are not bridged. Default: false |
| `force` | `boolean` | no | `false` | If true, deletes nodes the editor protects (CanUserDeleteNode false: a function entry, the entry and exit tunnels of a collapsed graph or macro). Deleting those can leave the Blueprint unable to compile. Default: false |
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Asset path of the Blueprint, e.g. /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door.BP_Door. With no target argument the focused graph is used; with blueprintPath alone, its focused graph or else its event graph. The result's 'target' says which graph was used. |
| `graphName` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Name of the graph (a function, macro, event graph or collapsed graph) in blueprintPath, or in the focused Blueprint without blueprintPath. AMBIGUOUS_GRAPH_NAME when two graphs share it: pass graphGuid then. |
| `graphGuid` | `string` | no |  | Optional. The graph's GUID (target.graphGuid of an earlier result; a function's functionGuid/guid is its graph GUID). Stable across renames and moves. Wins over graphName. |

Searches for specific nodes in a Blueprint graph (the one blueprintPath plus graphName or graphGuid name, else the focused graph) by keywords or node GUIDs. Returns matching nodes in N2C JSON format with full node and pin GUID information.

| yes | no | yes | no | no | yes | yes | yes |

| `searchType` | `string` | no | `"keyword"` | Type of search: 'keyword' or 'guid'. One of: `"keyword"`, `"guid"`. |
| `caseSensitive` | `boolean` | no | `false` | Whether keyword search is case-sensitive |
| `maxResults` | `number` | no | `50` | Maximum number of nodes to return |
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Asset path of the Blueprint, e.g. /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door.BP_Door. With no target argument the focused graph is used; with blueprintPath alone, its focused graph or else its event graph. The result's 'target' says which graph was used. |
| `graphName` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Name of the graph (a function, macro, event graph or collapsed graph) in blueprintPath, or in the focused Blueprint without blueprintPath. AMBIGUOUS_GRAPH_NAME when two graphs share it: pass graphGuid then. |
| `graphGuid` | `string` | no |  | Optional. The graph's GUID (target.graphGuid of an earlier result; a function's functionGuid/guid is its graph GUID). Stable across renames and moves. Wins over graphName. |

### set-input-pin-value

**Set an input pin's default value**

Sets the default value of an input pin on a Blueprint node of a graph (the one blueprintPath plus graphName or graphGuid name, else the focused graph). Only works on pins that accept default values (not exec, reference, or container pins). The engine checks the value first: one the pin refuses is an error and the old default stays. Enums take an entry name, display name or index. An empty value resets the pin to its default; newValue is what the pin holds afterwards. Refused with PIE_ACTIVE while a Play In Editor session runs; stop PIE first.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | yes | yes | no | no | no | no | yes |

Unreal MCP counterpart (UE 5.8): `BlueprintTools.set_pin_value`. Left to Unreal MCP by default when it runs in the same editor (Overlapping Tools).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nodeGuid` | `string` | yes |  |  |
| `pinGuid` | `string` | yes |  |  |
| `pinName` | `string` | no |  |  |

### create-local-variable

**Create a local variable**

Creates a new local variable in a Blueprint function (the one blueprintPath plus graphName or graphGuid name, else the focused function). The name is made unique against the Blueprint's members and the function's parameters and locals (a taken name gets a _0, _1... suffix; actualName is the name used). One undo removes it. For map variables: 'typeIdentifier' specifies the map's VALUE type, and 'mapKeyTypeIdentifier' (added by common schema utils) specifies the map's KEY type. Refused with PIE_ACTIVE while a Play In Editor session runs; stop PIE first.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | no | no | no | no | no | no | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `variableName` | `string` | yes |  | Name for the new local variable |
| `typeIdentifier` | `string` | yes |  | Type identifier for the variable's value. For non-container types, this is the variable's type (e.g., 'bool', 'FVector', '/Script/Engine.Actor'). Classes, structs and enums can be given by name, with or without the C++ prefix ('Actor', 'AActor', 'HitResult', 'FHitResult', 'ECollisionChannel', a user struct such as 'S_Loot'), or by path ('/Script/Engine.HitResult', '/Game/Data/S_Loot.S_Loot'); a name that matches more than one type needs its path. wildcard, exec and delegate types and C++ template spellings such as TArray&lt;...&gt; are refused. For 'array' or 'set' containers, this is the element type. For 'map' containers, this specifies the map's VALUE type; the KEY type is specified by 'mapKeyTypeIdentifier'. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | no | `""` | Optional default value for the variable |
| `tooltip` | `string` | no | `""` | Tooltip description for the variable |
| `containerType` | `string` | no | `"none"` | Container type for the variable (none, array, set, map). One of: `"none"`, `"array"`, `"set"`, `"map"`. |
| `mapKeyTypeIdentifier` | `string` | no | `""` | For 'map' containerType, this specifies the map's KEY type identifier (e.g., 'Name', 'int32', 'FString', '/Script/Engine.Actor', 'Guid'; the key must be hashable: bool, text and structs without a hash function are refused). This is required if containerType is 'map'. The map's VALUE type is specified by 'typeIdentifier'. Example: For TMap&lt;FName, FVector&gt;, 'typeIdentifier' would be 'FVector' and 'mapKeyTypeIdentifier' would be 'FName'. |
| `blueprintPath` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Asset path of the Blueprint, e.g. /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door.BP_Door. With no target argument the focused graph is used; with blueprintPath alone, its focused graph or else its event graph. The result's 'target' says which graph was used. |
| `graphName` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Name of the graph (a function, macro, event graph or collapsed graph) in blueprintPath, or in the focused Blueprint without blueprintPath. AMBIGUOUS_GRAPH_NAME when two graphs share it: pass graphGuid then. |
| `graphGuid` | `string` | no |  | Optional. The graph's GUID (target.graphGuid of an earlier result; a function's functionGuid/guid is its graph GUID). Stable across renames and moves. Wins over graphName. |

## FileSystemTools

Read text files and list folders inside the project directory.

### read-file

**Read a project text file**

Reads a text file in the Unreal Engine project, or in the translation output directory when that is outside the project. relativePath is relative to the project folder; an absolute path is accepted only inside those two folders. Only text files are read (source, config, JSON, CSV, Markdown, logs, ...): other types such as .uasset, .uexp, .png or .dll, and files with NUL bytes or invalid UTF-8, are refused. At most 500 KB of text comes back per call, in whole lines: truncated is true when the cap cut the read short, and nextOffset is the offset that continues it. offset and limit read a line range. Credential files (secrets.json, .env, Saved/NodeToCode/User, .git) are never readable.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |

Client hints: text results up to 200000 characters (`anthropic/maxResultSizeChars`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `relativePath` | `string` | yes |  | The file, relative to the project folder (for example "Config/DefaultEngine.ini"); an absolute path must be inside the project or the translation output directory |
| `offset` | `integer` | no |  | Optional. The line number to start at, 1-based (default 1) |
| `limit` | `integer` | no |  | Optional. The most lines to return (default: as many as fit in 500 KB) |

### read-path

**List a project directory**

Lists the files and folders directly inside a directory of the Unreal Engine project (not recursive), or of the translation output directory when that is outside the project. relativePath is relative to the project folder: "" or "." for the project folder, "Config", "Content/Blueprints"; an absolute path is accepted only inside those two folders. Results come in pages, folders first and then files, each sorted by name: total counts every entry, and when truncated is true pass nextCursor as cursor for the next page. filter keeps the names that match a wildcard such as "*.json". Credential folders (Saved/NodeToCode/User, .git) cannot be listed.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `relativePath` | `string` | yes |  | The directory, relative to the project folder ("" for the project folder); an absolute path must be inside the project or the translation output directory |
| `pageSize` | `integer` | no | `200` | Optional. Entries per page, 1 to 1000 (default 200) |
| `cursor` | `string` | no |  | Optional. The nextCursor of the previous page; leave it out for the first page |
| `filter` | `string` | no |  | Optional. A wildcard the names must match, * and ? (for example "*.json"), ignoring case; it applies to folders and files |

Returns `structuredContent` matching its `outputSchema` (in tools.generated.json).

## PythonTools

Run Python in the editor with the unreal module (only when the user allows MCP Python execution), and keep a library of reusable Python scripts to list, search, read, save and delete.

### delete-python-script

**Delete a library script**

Delete a Python script from the script library. This permanently removes both the script file and its registry entry. Use with caution - this action cannot be undone.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | yes | yes | no | no | no | yes | no |

Served only when the per-user Allow MCP Python Execution is on (off by default).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | The name of the script to delete. Use list-python-scripts or search-python-scripts to find the exact script name. |

### get-python-script

**Read a library script**

Get a Python script's full code and metadata by name. Returns the script code, description, tags, parameters, and usage stats. Use this to understand implementation details before extending or modifying a script. For just seeing importable functions (more token-efficient), use get-script-functions instead.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | The name of the script to retrieve. Use search-python-scripts or list-python-scripts to discover available script names. |

### get-script-functions

**List a library script's functions**

Get function signatures from a Python script using AST parsing (~80% more token-efficient than get-python-script). Returns function names, parameters, types, and docstrings WITHOUT full implementation code. Use this after search-python-scripts finds a partial match to see what functions can be imported. Then import in your code: 'from scripts.&lt;category&gt;.&lt;script_name&gt; import function_name'.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | The name of the script to analyze. Use search-python-scripts or list-python-scripts to find available script names. |

### list-python-scripts

**List library scripts**

List available Python scripts from the script library. Returns script names with metadata (description, tags, usage count). Use alongside search-python-scripts to discover reusable scripts before writing new code (DRY principle). Browse by category to find related utilities that can be imported and composed.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `category` | `string` | no |  | Filter scripts by category (e.g., 'gameplay', 'ui', 'utilities', 'animation'). Leave empty for all categories. Categories organize scripts for easier discovery and import. |
| `limit` | `integer` | no |  | Maximum number of scripts to return (default: 20, max: 100) |

### run-python

**Run Python in the editor**

Execute Python code in Unreal Engine's Python environment. WORKFLOW: 1) Search existing scripts first (search-python-scripts), 2) Use Context7 MCP to look up UE Python APIs (resolve-library-id with 'unreal-python-stubhub', then query-docs) - never guess signatures, 3) Import saved scripts: 'from scripts.&lt;category&gt;.&lt;name&gt; import func', 4) Use 'import nodetocode as n2c' for Blueprint utilities (get_focused_blueprint, compile_blueprint, save_blueprint, tag_graph), 5) Set 'result' variable to return structured data.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | yes | no | yes | no | no | yes | no |

Served only when the per-user Allow MCP Python Execution is on (off by default).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | `string` | yes |  | Python code to execute. Use 'import unreal' for UE APIs (verify signatures with Context7). Use 'import nodetocode as n2c' for Blueprint utilities. Import saved scripts: 'from scripts.&lt;category&gt;.&lt;script_name&gt; import function_name'. Set 'result = {...}' to return structured data. |
| `timeout` | `number` | no |  | Timeout in seconds (default: 60, max: 300) |

### save-python-script

**Save a library script**

Save a Python script to the script library for reuse. Stored in Content/Python/scripts/&lt;category&gt;/ and importable as 'from scripts.&lt;category&gt;.&lt;name&gt; import func'. Write modular scripts with focused functions, clear docstrings, and parameterized inputs. Every saved script grows the reusable toolkit for future tasks.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | yes | yes | no | no | no | yes | no |

Served only when the per-user Allow MCP Python Execution is on (off by default).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | Unique name for the script (alphanumeric and underscores only). Will be used as the filename and for retrieval. |
| `code` | `string` | yes |  | The Python code to save. Should be valid Python that can run in Unreal Engine's Python environment. Structure with reusable functions (def), docstrings, and parameters for flexibility. Avoid hardcoded values. |
| `description` | `string` | yes |  | Brief description of what the script does. Used for search. |
| `tags` | `array<string>` | no |  | Tags for categorizing and searching the script (e.g., ['blueprint', 'variables', 'health']). |
| `category` | `string` | no |  | Category folder for organization (default: 'general'). Examples: 'gameplay', 'ui', 'utilities', 'animation'. |

### search-python-scripts

**Search library scripts**

CALL THIS FIRST before writing any Python code. Search for existing scripts to reuse. Returns matching scripts sorted by relevance. If exact match found: execute it with run-python. If partial match found: use get-script-functions to see importable functions, then compose. Only write new code if no relevant scripts exist.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | `string` | yes |  | Search query with keywords from the task. Matches against script names, descriptions, and tags. Case-insensitive partial matching. Try multiple relevant keywords if first search yields no results. |
| `limit` | `integer` | no |  | Maximum number of results to return (default: 10, max: 50) |

## TranslationTools

Translate the focused Blueprint graph into C++, Python, C#, JavaScript, Swift or pseudocode with the LLM provider configured in Project Settings, and read the available providers, target languages and output folder.

### get-available-llm-providers

**List LLM providers**

Returns the LLM providers available for Blueprint translation: cloud providers with an API key (saved in Project Settings or from an environment variable; keySource says which, never the key) and the local providers.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |

No arguments.

Returns `structuredContent` matching its `outputSchema` (in tools.generated.json).

### get-available-translation-targets

**List translation languages**

Returns the list of programming languages that NodeToCode can translate Blueprints into, including metadata about each language.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |

No arguments.

Returns `structuredContent` matching its `outputSchema` (in tools.generated.json).

### get-translation-output-directory

**Show the translation output folder**

Returns the translation output directory configuration from NodeToCode settings. Shows whether a custom directory is set or if the default location is being used. Every translation is saved there as a run folder with a manifest.json: from the editor's NodeToCode window, translate-batch, translate-focused-blueprint and the Python API.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no | no | yes | yes |

No arguments.

Returns `structuredContent` matching its `outputSchema` (in tools.generated.json).

### translate-batch

**Translate many Blueprint graphs**

Translates many Blueprint graphs with an LLM provider in one call, with no Blueprint editor open and without changing focus: one LLM request per graph, one after another. Select the graphs with targets [{blueprintPath, graphName?, graphGuid?}] (a target with only blueprintPath translates every graph of that Blueprint that has nodes) or with a tag and/or category. It can take minutes: send params._meta.progressToken to receive notifications/progress, and cancel with notifications/cancelled (the request in flight stops at once, the rest are skipped). The result lists every graph with its status, the folder its files were saved in (under the translation output directory, BatchTranslation_&lt;time&gt;), its code while the whole result stays under about 20000 tokens (else read the files) and, for a failure, the typed error. Only one batch runs at a time. Assets that are not Blueprints are refused per target (UNSUPPORTED_ASSET_TYPE).

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | no | no | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `targets` | `array<object>` | no |  | The graphs to work on: [{blueprintPath, graphName?, graphGuid?}]. Give targets, or tag and/or category, not both. At most 50 graphs per call. A path that is not a Blueprint (a Material, a Data Asset) fails with UNSUPPORTED_ASSET_TYPE. |
| `tag` | `string` | no |  | Instead of targets: every graph with this tag (tag-blueprint-graph, list-blueprint-tags), in category when given. |
| `category` | `string` | no |  | Instead of targets: every graph tagged in this category (with tag: that tag in this category). |
| `language` | `string` | no |  | Optional: target language ID as get-available-translation-targets lists it (e.g. 'cpp', 'python'; case-insensitive). Default: the settings' Target Language; an unknown ID is an error. |
| `provider` | `string` | no |  | Optional: LLM provider ID as get-available-llm-providers lists it (e.g. 'anthropic', 'ollama'; case-insensitive). Default: the settings' provider; an unknown ID is an error. |
| `model` | `string` | no |  | Optional: model ID. Default: the provider's model in settings. An ID NodeToCode does not list for a cloud provider is still sent, with a note in the result's warnings. |

### translate-focused-blueprint

**Translate the focused Blueprint graph**

Translates the currently focused Blueprint graph using an LLM provider and returns the translation as this call's result. The focused Blueprint is the Blueprint editor the user last activated or that open-blueprint-asset last opened. It can take minutes: send params._meta.progressToken to receive notifications/progress while it runs. The translation is also saved to the translation output directory (get-translation-output-directory) as a run folder with a manifest.json. The result's structuredContent is the translation (graphs with their code, usage); one larger than 200,000 characters is saved under Saved/NodeToCode/Exports/Translations instead and the result lists its graphs, savedTo and a resource_link to the file.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running | Untrusted text | During PIE | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | no | no | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

Client hints: text results up to 200000 characters (`anthropic/maxResultSizeChars`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | `string` | no |  | Optional: LLM provider ID as get-available-llm-providers lists it (e.g., 'openai', 'anthropic', 'ollama'; case-insensitive). Uses settings default if empty; an unknown ID is an error. |
| `model` | `string` | no |  | Optional: Specific model ID. Uses provider's default from settings if empty. An ID NodeToCode does not list for a cloud provider is still sent, with a note in the result's warnings array. |
| `language` | `string` | no |  | Optional: Target language ID as get-available-translation-targets lists it (e.g., 'cpp', 'python'; case-insensitive). Uses settings default if empty; an unknown ID is an error. |

Returns `structuredContent` matching its `outputSchema` (in tools.generated.json).

## Tool search meta-tools

With Tool Exposure set to Tool search, `tools/list` holds only these three, named and shaped like UE 5.8's tool search. They reach every tool the profile serves.

### call_tool

**Call a tool**

Call a NodeToCode tool by name with its arguments and return its result. Use list_toolsets and describe_toolset to find tool names and input schemas. Long-running tools report progress and can be cancelled as when called directly.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no | yes | no | yes | no |

Client hints: kept loaded when a client defers tools (`anthropic/alwaysLoad`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `toolset_name` | `string` | no |  | Optional. Name of the toolset that holds the tool, as list_toolsets shows it. |
| `tool_name` | `string` | yes |  | Name of the tool to call, as describe_toolset shows it. |
| `arguments` | `object` | no |  | Arguments for the tool, matching the input schema describe_toolset shows. Defaults to an empty object. |

### describe_toolset

**Describe a toolset**

Get a toolset's tools: each tool's name, description, input schema and behaviour hints, as JSON. Use list_toolsets for the toolset names.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no |

Client hints: kept loaded when a client defers tools (`anthropic/alwaysLoad`).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `toolset_name` | `string` | yes |  | Name of the toolset to describe, as list_toolsets shows it. |

### list_toolsets

**List toolsets**

List NodeToCode's toolsets with their names and descriptions. Call describe_toolset on one to see its tools, then call_tool to run a tool.

| Read-only | Destructive | Idempotent | Open world | Long-running |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | yes | no | no |

Client hints: kept loaded when a client defers tools (`anthropic/alwaysLoad`).

No arguments.
